findings.title: Tool-runtime visit no longer suppresses actual link-library byte/admission checks
findings.confirmed_old_behavior: Old Inputs.seen deduplicated only by canonical path. Earlier clang/ld runtime file(false) visits could cause later actual library/script file(true) visits to return before full bytes, size/ELF/archive/script admission and DT_NEEDED collection.
findings.fix_review: Inputs.seen now keys canonical path plus role. A true/content-bound visit executes its original full fs::read/hash and format/dependency admission even if false/tool identity was already visited or memoized. The final DT_NEEDED closure admits only a matching content_bound=true path; runtime metadata identity alone cannot satisfy it. All candidate search roots, libraries, scripts, current argv/env and external discovery remain current.
findings.counterexamples_reviewed: The first regression accepts unsupported bytes in false role and then requires the same true-role input to reject, asserting the actual bytes read. A supported GNU-build-ID ELF fixture has zero tool SHA-fallback bytes while two separate true-role traversals each hash its full payload; tool memo cannot absorb that work. Both tests passed in the 217-test backend result.
findings.evidence_limit: This repairs the independently demonstrated skipped required admission. No stale ELF was independently reproduced on the controlled installed native toolchain, and none is claimed.

boundary_review.assessment: Session-local memo keys canonical paths and a complete Unix stamp: dev/inode/mode/uid/gid/link count/length, modified time and nanosecond mtime/ctime. Lookup opens the actual file first, compares fresh path metadata to that handle, performs old installed identity on a miss, then rechecks the same handle, original canonical resolution and current path before using or publishing. Only successful final checks insert; failures cannot publish a new memo entry. Non-Unix does not reuse. At most 512 tool owners are cached. The trusted installed-tool model is explicit and does not become content proof for libraries.

boundary_review.area: Semantic-v6 decode order and current fingerprint
boundary_review.assessment: Manifest layout validates every binding flag/span ordering and descriptor aggregate lengths before any child load. Each child hash/length is checked, then original bounded raw module/candidate/metadata decoding completes. These decoders do not validate semantic module fingerprint. rebind checks exact ordered function IDs/count, exact-bound function span equality, or canonical FileId(0),0,length; all canonical function/local/instruction spans must fit that envelope and are restored with checked addition. Only after complete rebinding does the pair return to current source/target/fingerprint checks and independent Verify. Source errors and rejected candidates retain existing clear/restart/fresh behavior; cancellation is never retried.

v6 selects a separate namespace/key version from v5. Items remain immutable content-addressed raw bytes; original guarded namespace writes, cancellation and manifest-last atomic publication remain. Current/previous publication fields are replaced, and session clear resets them; checkpoint-shared fragments and per-file budgets still do not imply an all-history/global byte bound.
